samples.summary: `COOKIE_SECURE` now feeds `cliLoginAvailable`, an out-of-diff consumer of `secureCookies` whose question is "can this origin hold a cookie an attacker cannot plant?" — the override answers a different question and moves that gate in both directions
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:216 `return secureCookies(configService) || loopbackCallback(configService);`, consumed at github-auth.guard.ts:514 to throw `BadRequestException('Command-line sign-in requires an https server')`. Before this delta that predicate was derived from the callback URL scheme only. Now: (a) an operator who sets `COOKIE_SECURE=false` on a genuinely https deployment (e.g. to work around a cookie problem) silently disables `wafflebase login` for every non-loopback deployment — the CLI gets a 400 that names https, on an https server, with no log; (b) `COOKIE_SECURE=true` on a real plain-http origin makes `cliLoginAvailable` return true, starting the CLI consent flow on cleartext where the `wafflebase_cli_confirm` cookie the gate rests on is plantable — the exact case the comment at lines 208-213 says is refused rather than started. The fix belongs on the new code: `cliLoginAvailable` should consult the derived origin scheme, not the operator's cookie-attribute override.

samples.summary: Logout's `clearCookie` now inherits `COOKIE_SECURE`, so `COOKIE_SECURE=true` on an origin actually served over http leaves the session cookie in the browser at sign-out
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:474-476 clears `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh` with `this.baseCookieOptions()`, whose `secure` is now `secureCookies()` and therefore operator-settable. A `Set-Cookie` carrying `Secure` sent from a plain-http origin is dropped by the browser, so the expiring cookie never lands and the previously-set session cookie survives logout. The pre-delta derivation could only produce `secure: true` on an origin that had declared itself https; the new override can produce it on an origin that is not. Same class as the `Secure`-on-http dead-login the PR describes, but on the revocation path rather than the login path, so it fails quietly instead of loudly.

Now: (a) an operator who sets `COOKIE_SECURE=false` on a genuinely https deployment (e.g. to work around a cookie problem) silently disables `wafflebase login` for every non-loopback deployment — the CLI gets a 400 that names https, on an https server, with no log; (b) `COOKIE_SECURE=true` on a real plain-http origin makes `cliLoginAvailable` return true, starting the CLI consent flow on cleartext where the `wafflebase_cli_confirm` cookie the gate rests on is plantable — the exact case the comment at lines 208-213 says is refused rather than started. verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. `secureCookies()` (github-auth.guard.ts:158-171) now returns the operator's `COOKIE_SECURE` value at lines 159-160 before deriving anything from `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL`'s scheme. `cliLoginAvailable()` at github-auth.guard.ts:215-216 is exactly `secureCookies(configService) || loopbackCallback(configService)`, and its sole consumer is the reachable CLI entry path in `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` (github-auth.guard.ts:507-518), which throws `BadRequestException('Command-line sign-in requires an https server')`. So an out-of-diff consumer whose stated contract (doc comment at 196-213: "every other plain-http origin is refused rather than started") is about the origin's scheme is now driven by a cookie-attribute override, flipping a security gate in both directions on reachable configurations. No refutation ground holds: the code is present as quoted (not `not-present`); grepping `cliLoginAvailable|Command-line sign-in|mode === 'cli'` finds only guard.ts:514 and an unrelated post-callback branch at auth.controller.ts:319, so no other guard makes it unreachable (not `already-guarded`); and a behaviour change to an exported symbol reaching an unreconciled out-of-diff consumer is precisely this lens's lane, scored major for a caller left inconsistent by a changed contract (not `out-of-scope`). Supporting evidence that the consumer was not reconciled: packages/backend/README.md:39-44 and packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:133-139 document `COOKIE_SECURE` only as a cookie-attribute override, while self-hosting.md:128-131 still describes CLI availability as a function of the callback URL scheme. I note the `COOKIE_SECURE=false` direction is arguably self-consistent (loginCookieName at line 238 does drop `__Host-` in that case, so refusing CLI login is coherent) and the `true`-on-plain-http direction may fail closed since browsers reject `Secure` cookies over cleartext — but that is inference about intent and browser behaviour, not a code-level counterexample, and the error text and documented contract are still wrong for a reachable config. Uncertainty keeps the finding.

verdict.reason: The cited code exists (clearAuthCookies at auth.controller.ts:473-477 uses baseCookieOptions(), whose secure is secureCookies() at 534-538, now operator-settable at github-auth.guard.ts:158-160), but the described failure cannot occur. The identical baseCookieOptions() is spread into the only setter of these cookies (setAuthCookies, auth.controller.ts:479-499), and grep across packages/ shows no other writer of wafflebase_session/wafflebase_refresh (res.cookie( hits: auth.controller.ts:484, 492; github-auth.guard.ts:657/686 are the separate login-state cookies). Secure is therefore symmetric between set and clear: with COOKIE_SECURE=true on an origin actually served over http, the login Set-Cookie is dropped by the browser for exactly the same reason, so no session cookie is ever stored and nothing survives logout — the deployment fails loudly at login, not quietly at revocation. The finding's premise that pre-delta secure:true required a self-declared https origin is also wrong: github-auth.guard.ts:170 returns true from NODE_ENV==='production' with no callback URL, on any scheme. The only reachable variant needs an operator to flip COOKIE_SECURE mid-session, which is inherent to any config-derived Secure flag and pre-dates the delta. Under the blast-radius rubric there is additionally no unupdated caller or bypass: the clearer and the setter share the one helper the diff changed.
